notes: Independent Youngstown ceramics maker founded 1967 by Roger and Gloria Jones, partly employee-owned via ESOP; Business Journal Daily reported 107 employees in Aug 2017 (101 in Dec 2016), matching Form 5500 counts of 108-109.

JobsOhio release (Mar 2025) says the 2008 spin-off of Alex Products has more than 200 employees; privately held by the Von Deylen family during the grant year, then acquired by Array Technologies (NM, public) in Q3 2025, after the grant (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1820721/000119312525142342/d931026dex991.htm).

Independent woman- and minority-owned steel fabricator in Cincinnati; JobsOhio's 2021 success story calls it a relatively small company and it received the Small Business (Inclusion) Grant, with 27 jobs retained in JobsOhio's project report.

No release, news story or working company site found (JobsOhio sitemap, Google News RSS, guessed domains); bucket rests on the Form 5500 counts (39 in 2019, 71 in 2023) and 33 jobs retained, with no sign of a parent. Schedule I cash of $899,641 exceeds the $100,000 JobsOhio commitment, which is worth checking.

parent: Otto Egelhof GmbH & Co. KG (EGELHOF Group)
notes: Toledo plant (founded 2005) of the family-owned EGELHOF group of Fellbach, Germany; the group site says 9 sites and 600 employees today, and the 2016 figure was not found, so the bucket assumes a similar size. The site says EGELHOF Controls has since stopped production and operates as a sales company, EGELHOF USA.

Los Angeles-area web-to-print company (Van Nuys/Sherman Oaks) with Ohio plants in Brook Park and Solon; Form 5500 shows 1,364 plan participants in 2023. PE-owned: H.I.G. Capital 2017-2021, then sold in Dec 2021 to an affiliate of Sycamore Partners, which also owns Staples.

parent: Interstate-McBee (McBee Supply Corp. / Interstate Diesel Service, Buescher family)
notes: McBee Supply is the distribution arm of Cleveland's family-founded Interstate-McBee diesel parts group; its careers page says 400+ employees at six U.S. locations (current, not grant year), and JobsOhio lists 272 jobs retained in Ohio. Near the 500 line, so a skeptic could push it up a bucket.

TransDigm's FY2019 10-K calls AeroControlex Group a wholly-owned subsidiary of TransDigm Inc. and reports about 18,300 employees at Sept. 30, 2019, with headquarters in Cleveland; the EIN is on EDGAR as a guarantor co-registrant. Founded-in-Ohio is from general background (TransDigm formed in Cleveland in 1993), not a fetched source.

Private, employee-owned pigment-dispersion maker founded in Sandusky in 1975, with plants in Tennessee, Shanghai and Italy (Colorificio Migliavacca, bought 2022). No headcount found; U.S. Form 5500 shows 99 participants in 2023, and the foreign plants likely push the worldwide total just over 100, so the bucket could be <100.

Azusa, Calif. cosmetic-packaging maker with factories in Asia and U.S. contract facilities; JobsOhio's 2021 releases give only 135 planned Defiance jobs and no company headcount. The size of the Asian factories is unknown, so the true bucket could be 500-4999; ownership of those factories was not confirmed.

Services arm of Core Specialty Insurance Holdings, a private insurer formed in 2020 from the StarStone U.S. business and headquartered in Cincinnati; Form 5500 shows 750 participants in 2023. No controlling owner: Enstar's 10-K reports a 19.9% equity-method stake, with the rest held by investors such as SkyKnight and Arch.

A Cleveland holding company that got only a $250,000 Revitalization Grant with zero jobs retained, so it looks like a property-owning entity; the name may refer to the Cleveland Industrial Innovation Center, but that link is unconfirmed. The JobsOhio sitemap, Google News RSS, EDGAR and guessed domains named no developer or operator.

Appears to be an independent wine shop or bar in Over-the-Rhine, Cincinnati; the only signals are the $40,000 Inclusion (small business) Grant and 3 jobs retained. Google News RSS found nothing and winehouseotr.com is now a parked domain, so no source confirmed owner or size.

Independent Cincinnati development and construction management firm (the company site and local press describe its townhome projects), classed as an operating business, not a single-project LLC. The site gives no headcount; the size comes from the Inclusion (small business) Grant and 4 jobs retained.

Fifth-generation family-owned highway guardrail and steel roll-former headquartered in the Canton area; the history page traces it to a galvanizing works founded in New York in 1896. Form 5500 shows 265 participants in 2023; it added an Alabama plant around 2022, which is likely covered by the same plan.

The London, Ohio headlamp plant is the U.S. arm of Tokyo-listed Stanley Electric; Wikipedia gives 16,687 consolidated employees at March 31, 2018. The U.S. unit's own Form 5500 showed 996 participants in 2015; the parent's annual securities report would support an A grade but was not fetched.

Privately held transformer supplier founded in 2015 and headquartered in Battle Ground, Wash., with plants in Greer, S.C. (the Schedule I address) and an Ohio site opened in 2023. The company site now claims 400+ employees; Form 5500 showed 184 participants in 2023, so it was in the 100-499 range in the grant year.

Public community college in Zanesville and Cambridge, founded in 1969 as Muskingum Area Technical College, with about 1,671 students in fall 2023. No staff count was found; 100-499 employees is an estimate based on enrollment.

Grant years span an ownership change: zulily (Seattle, 2,907 employees per its 10-K for FY2014, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1478484/000147848415000018/zu-12282014x10k.htm) was independent for the FY2015 payment, then Liberty Interactive bought it in Oct 2015 and owned it for the FY2017 payment (subsidiaries had about 21,000 employees at end of 2016). Either parent is 5000+.
